findings.title: The installed create helper is rejected by unchanged closed ActiveCatalog v2 admission
findings.trigger: Install the frozen new helper as setup_all does, then start/admit the browser Store or make any active browser read.
findings.proof: ActiveCatalog v2 still has exactly20 functions with LIMIT21. Its name-prefix query includes mixer_browser_create_active_load, making21 rows; require!(length(rows)==20) fails. Its separate callable-definer escape check also sees the new browser_writer-owned function. R2112 does not modify ActiveCatalog. Store selects version2 before any relation/create compatibility check. The one SQL-free source control reproduced this exact count predicate; no SQL/runtime was run.
findings.impact: The create-enabled installation cannot pass browser admission; it blocks startup/PKCE/HTTP creation and the existing read route on that installation.
findings.minimal_fix: Introduce an explicitly selected create-enabled exact function/ACL manifest including the helper and correct counts/bounds. Keep the legacy20-function manifest for read-only installations; validate owner, complete signature, body, five retained settings, return/argument types and exact execution ACL/grantor. Extend both functions and escape-path validation; do not ignore all extra browser functions. Targeted source review then actual startup/create/GET test.

findings.title: Create catalog admission does not seal the RLS policies that make UPDATE grants lock-only
findings.trigger: A misprovisioned/drifted catalog changes ALTER POLICY build_create_lock ON public.mixer_builds WITH CHECK (true), or adds a permissive policy for mixer_build_create.
findings.proof: compatibility! inspects pg_policy only for PUBLIC role0. It never reads the create policies names, commands, permissiveness, USING or WITH CHECK; role-specific mutations therefore leave every tested catalog field unchanged. The SELECT and UPDATE grants are present, and changing this WITH CHECK removes the explicit prohibition on changing a scoped build row under valid create context. Existing enclosing RelationCatalog seals its nine browser relations; BuildCatalogAdmission seals application policies/the catalog definer, neither seals these three new create-policy surfaces. This is a source-level catalog-admission counterexample, not a demonstrated live database exploit.
findings.impact: The constrained role can be admitted while its intended lock-only/writer boundary has drifted. A successful happy-path create does not qualify fail-closed SQL policy admission.
findings.minimal_fix: Add a bounded exact policy manifest for the three touched tables, including roles, commands, permissiveness, USING/WITH CHECK and absence of extras. Check the exact create-role table/column/sequence ACLs and grantors needed for that boundary. Also bind the new SECURITY DEFINER helper settings/signature/ACL, which compatibility! currently does not seal. Use narrow negative catalog mutations in the fresh root campaign, with an independent targeted review of changed rows.

findings.title: The job-failure telemetry handler can detach and the expiry assertion does not prove post-insert rollback
findings.trigger: The intended oban_jobs INSERT fails under the owned table lock, then the same test runs the short-identity expiry control.
findings.proof: observe/4 branches on the INSERT query text without requiring m.result to be {:ok,...}, then query!s the same transaction. After a PostgreSQL statement error that transaction is aborted, so the query can raise. The pinned telemetry source catches handler exceptions and detaches the handler (telemetry.erl201-205). The expiry case only accepts401/503 and unchanged counts; it never requires a successful job_insert event for that request or checks handler survival. Rejection before the job INSERT can satisfy those assertions. This path has not been executed by this reviewer.
findings.impact: The claimed post-job final-expiry rollback control can be unexercised, or a detached observer can make the later test fail for instrumentation reasons.
findings.minimal_fix: Only query the backend after a successful INSERT telemetry result. Record failed INSERT evidence without issuing SQL into an aborted transaction. Drain/correlate events per request, assert no handler-failure event and handler still attached, require a successful job insertion before the expiry barrier, then assert the final refusal and rollback counts. Assert the blocked-job control actually reached the intended failing INSERT.
